newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks close up with late rally.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks close up with late rally.

text.p: South African stocks closed up on Thursday as a late rally spurred by futures trade in the industrials sector overcame a market initially hamstrung by a sickly-looking golds sector.

A rush of futures business, as dealers settled positions ahead of the close-out of the September contract early next week, dragged the market out of its noon doldrums and created a healthy volume of upwards moving trade.
The all-share index closed up 34.6 points at 6,814.6 as industrials put on 48.8 points to 8,040.7.
But news was less rosy in the golds market.

A swift decline in the morning wiped out most of Wednesday's gains as market nerves started to become frayed ahead of a crucial meeting on Friday of the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The IMF is mulling the possible sale of five million ounces of gold to raise funds to help developing countries.

Dealers also said there had been a reaction to bullion's refusal to move upwards on the news of the latest outbreak of U.S.-Iraqi tension in the Gulf. Such disruption is usually good news for the gold price.
The late rally did help the gold share index off its day's low, but failed to pull it into the black. The sector ended down 4.2 points at 1,743.0.
